decima.question: Will the mean absolute error across this 50 m density gap be at most 0.05 g/cm³?

thirty_seconds: We hid one real 50 m stretch of bulk density in each of the 20 FORCE test wells. The best fill came from Mistral's Timestral-5M, frozen, reading the other logs across the gap: 0.033 g/cm³ mean error, 45 % better than a straight line (0.061), better in 18 of 20 wells, 16 of 20 gaps within 0.05. From the density log alone the models tie: Timestral 0.047, IBM TTM-R3 0.048, TSPulse 0.049 (TTM − Timestral +0.0007, 95 % CI -0.0023 to +0.0045). So the gain is the other logs (-0.0135, 95 % CI -0.0221 to -0.0062), not the model. The brief's laptop fine-tune of the IBM heads (early-stopped after 75–125 updates, 5 s or less on a laptop GPU) changed TTM error by -0.0006 (95 % CI -0.0017 to +0.0004) and TSPulse by -0.0001. A stronger fine-tune afterwards (broader unfreezing, 8× more training gaps, longer schedule, chosen on B only): TTM-R3 fine-tune (heads) (1.08 M weights trained, 1800 updates, 3.5 min) 0.047, -0.0010 vs frozen (95 % CI -0.0046 to +0.0028); TSPulse fine-tune (whole model) (1.07 M weights trained, 2900 updates, 2.7 min) 0.046, -0.0035 vs frozen (95 % CI -0.0070 to -0.0008). Gardner from sonic alone is worse than the line (0.100); corrected by the flank residual it reaches 0.056. Timestral's nominal 90 % band covers only 46 % of the hidden samples; the D-calibrated Granite bands cover 96 %. For each gap a small calibrated rule (Numeric logistic) says whether the TSPulse quick-tune fill is within 0.05 g/cm³: at p ≥ 0.80 it accepted 7 of 20 gaps with 0 false accepts and sent 13 to review; Brier 0.158 vs 0.261 for the base rate. A small verifier model (Decima-small) reading the same facts as text accepted 0 gaps (p_pass 0.47–0.53, Brier 0.239): its probabilities hardly vary and on the 236 development gaps its ranking is near chance, so it never reaches the 0.80 bar. Refitted on each model's own fills, the same rule ranks gaps with test AUC 0.75–0.91; adding two gamma-ray features (GR is measured inside the gap) lowers its test Brier for 10 of 10 models.
